content.content:
The detail panel's markup and its stylesheet share one vocabulary for the two cases of a listed entry, and this decision fixes that vocabulary: the names "detail__entry" and "detail__entry--inert", and which case each name denotes.


Both are classes carried by the element that holds the entry's id text — the element showing the bare id a relationship section lists (rmovtvkt). A listed entry whose id names a node document carries "detail__entry". A listed entry whose id names none — the entry an id naming no node document is listed as (rusopkql) — carries "detail__entry--inert".


The mapping is exhaustive and exclusive over listed entries: exactly one of the two classes is on any listed entry, never neither and never both. No entry is left without a class while its siblings carry one, so no listed entry falls through to whatever an unclassed element would be styled as, and no entry carries both names, so the two cases are never marked at once and the markup cannot be read as either case or both. Every listed id is marked with the name that says which case it is.


The stylesheet's rules select those two classes: whatever rules the stylesheet carries for a listed entry are written against "detail__entry" and against "detail__entry--inert", so the class an entry carries is what decides which of the stylesheet's entry rules reach it. That selection is the whole of this decision's claim about the stylesheet. It fixes no declaration — no colour or colour role, no pointer cursor, no hover marking, no focus indicator, no text decoration, underline or outline, no line thickness, no weight or spacing. Whether the rules for the two names declare the same thing, different things or nothing at all, and which elements or states those rules further select, are the stylesheet's own decisions, each settled where it is owned.


The names are fixed exactly as written and are not to be multiplied: this decision adds no third class, no further modifier to either name, no data attribute, no element id and no other hook, and no nesting of one class inside the other's block. "detail__entry--inert" is one class name in full, not "detail__entry" with a separate modifier class applied beside it — an entry that names no node carries "detail__entry--inert" and does not also carry "detail__entry". A carrier that needs a finer distinction states that as its own decision rather than spelling a new name out of these two.


Nothing here changes what an entry shows or what activating it does. The entry's text stays the bare id the selected node's field holds, with no label, substitute or annotation added by the class; the class names the element and adds nothing to it. What the two cases look like is not decided here either: whether a listed entry reads as a link, which colour role an id naming no node takes, which cues it shows and which it abstains from are each another decision's, and this one neither presumes nor rules out any of them. The classes are carried whether or not a rule declares anything for them; a class is the name of a case, not a promise that a declaration follows, so a stylesheet abstention on either case changes no entry's markup, and what any rule should declare stays outside this decision.
content.rationale:
Two carriers have to say the same two names: the panel carrier, which puts a class on each listed entry's id element in its markup, and the stylesheet carrier, whose rules select those classes. Each is a later refine of a node already in the graph, and the panel carrier's node (tpztomkv) is newer in history than the stylesheet carrier's (rtlotqvy). A stylesheet that quoted the panel's class names would therefore need a depends_on edge toward a node that comes after it, inverting the edge; a panel that quoted the stylesheet's names would carry the same inversion the other way. Fixing the vocabulary in one node below both gives each carrier a forward edge to here instead, so neither has to name the other and the two still meet on the same two strings. That is the whole reason this node exists: it is the meeting point the edge order could not otherwise provide.

The mapping has to be stated, not merely the names. mwwxxzyk commits a listed entry to reading as a link, rusopkql keeps the entry whose id names no node document listed among its siblings and inert, and mplxzxnm draws that entry's id text in the muted secondary colour role. Those decisions settle behaviour and one colour role; none of them says what the two cases are called, and mwwxxzyk expressly leaves the class vocabulary to another decision. If the carriers were handed two bare names, each would have to guess which name means which case, and a guess that crossed would put the link-look rules on the inert entries and the mute on the followable ones — a panel that looks exactly inverted while every node is satisfied. The mapping fixes which name denotes which case once, so the carrier that emits the class and the carrier that selects the class cannot disagree about it.

Exactness is part of the vocabulary rather than a detail of it. A vocabulary that allowed neither class leaves listed entries unclassed, and each carrier would then default on its own: the markup by emitting nothing, the stylesheet by styling every listed entry with whatever rules are not class-scoped. One that allowed both makes the two cases overlap in the markup, so both rule sets reach an entry and no rule can say which case it is looking at. Exactly one of the two on every listed entry is what lets a single class name be read as the answer to "which case is this entry", which is the only thing the stylesheet needs from the markup. Spelling "detail__entry--inert" as one name rather than as "detail__entry" plus a modifier is the same point: the BEM-looking double dash is a name, and applying it alongside "detail__entry" would silently reintroduce the both-cases state.

Stopping at the names is what keeps the appearance decisions decidable. Each thing a reviewer would want to check about how an entry looks — the colour role of the followable entry, the pointer cursor, the hover underline, the focus outline, and the cases where a cue is deliberately withheld — is a declaration in the stylesheet, checkable by reading the rule that carries it. Fixed here, those declarations would have to be restated or contradicted by the nodes that own them, and a single node would then answer two questions at once. Left open, each is a class name the later decision can point at and one property it can settle, and a carrier is still free to declare nothing for a name — which is why the presence of the class is stated independently of any declaration existing for it: an abstention is a decision about a rule, not about whether an entry is marked as the case it is.

Nothing here reaches past the vocabulary into behaviour or text. The entry stays the bare id mwwxxzyk and mplxzxnm fix, the inert entry stays listed and stays inert as rusopkql settles, and whether either entry is followed or muted in colour remains theirs; this node names the cases, and the cases are what those prerequisites already described.
